items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I remember this teacher very fondly, Miss Hammond.

ctx.x: We were now in Bromley. You asked about my musical influence. That was it, was actually hearing my mother play. I don’t have to go the piano and illustrate. I can tell you exactly what I heard that seemed to me to be something that I should follow up. It was a Chopin waltz in A-flat. I remember trying to play it and being at the piano from then on. That was my prime place to be at age probably three or something like that. Then when I went to kindergarten . . . Oh, I’ve got to keep up with all these moves. We had…
That’s fine. We’re getting a lot of these things that will just . . . the questions will lead to a lot of other information that we can just draw upon, ask questions
